members.name: Noah Nelson
members.bio:
Homeschooling played a vital role in shaping Mr. Nelson’s character and love for learning. From an early age, his mother cultivated in him and his siblings a deep appreciation for literature by reading to them daily, while his great-aunt’s phonics curriculum laid the foundation for a lifelong love of reading. Growing up on the family farm further enriched this education, instilling responsibility, diligence, and the value of hard work. Noah also gained practical experience in stewardship and discipline by managing a small roadside stand that sold the farm’s fruits and vegetables. 

A hallmark of Noah’s homeschooling experience was the consistent integration of Scripture into every subject. He was taught to view all of life through the lens of God’s ownership of all things—that every field of study, including mathematics, is grounded in the reality of God’s existence and character. Without God, mathematics and reason would not exist, for they reflect the order and logic of a sovereign and rational Creator. Mr. Nelson is a graduate of Colorado Heritage Education School System and was blessed that the philosophy of Christian education he received at CHESS mirrored and came alongside the Christian education he received at home.

For Mr. Nelson, homeschooling is significant not only for its academic benefits but also for its theological foundation: it preserves the God-given responsibility of parents to make sure that they themselves (or those they authorize) train their children in the nurture and admonition of the Lord.

Among his favorite portions of Scripture are the Psalms, with Psalm 103 being one of his favorites. Outside of his studies and work, Noah enjoys photography, classical music, and reading.

Mr. Nelson is currently prayerfully considering pursuing a master’s degree in Christian education.
